question: What is the primary purpose of the Primary Health Care workforce in Nigeria?

options.A: To provide highly specialized surgical care at tertiary medical centers
options.B: To bring comprehensive, equitable, and cost-effective health services close to the people
options.C: To exclusively manage administrative policies for the Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: To replace traditional medicine without community involvement

explanation: The PHC workforce is specifically designed to deliver promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative services as close as possible to where people live and work. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is it important for nursing students to understand the different cadres of PHC workers?

options.A: To ensure effective delegation, coordination, and optimal health outcomes in resource-limited settings
options.B: So they can take over the administrative duties of local government chairmen
options.C: To eliminate the need for community participation in health programs
options.D: To practice major surgical procedures independently at the grassroots level

explanation: Understanding the distinct skills and scopes of practice of various PHC cadres ensures proper coordination, delegation, and teamwork to achieve the best health outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes the primary clinical role of a Community Physician in the PHC system?

options.B: Diagnosing and managing complex medical cases beyond the scope of nurses and CHEWs
options.C: Handling only administrative financial auditing for local health clinics
options.D: Replacing traditional birth attendants in remote villages

explanation: Community physicians utilize their medical training to handle complex clinical cases that exceed the scope of practice of other frontline PHC workers. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h2)

question: How do community physicians support other members of the PHC team?

options.A: By providing clinical mentorship, technical supervision, and continuous guidance
options.B: By taking over all nursing duties in the facility
options.C: By isolating themselves in administrative offices away from clinical staff

explanation: Community physicians provide technical supervision and clinical mentorship to ensure high standards of care across the multidisciplinary PHC team. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary organizational role of a Community Health Officer (CHO) in a PHC facility?

options.A: Managing facility operations, supervising junior staff, and coordinating PHC programs
options.B: Performing major surgical operations independently at secondary hospitals
options.C: Focusing solely on international health policy formulation
options.D: Delivering babies exclusively without any managerial duties

explanation: CHOs serve as middle-level managers responsible for overseeing facility operations, supervising junior workers, and implementing primary health care programs. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h3)

question: Who do CHOs typically bridge between within the Nigerian health system?

options.A: Lower-level health workers like CHEWs and higher medical authorities
options.C: Secondary school teachers and university professors
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies and international donors

explanation: CHOs act as a crucial link between junior health workers (such as CHEWs) and higher medical management or authorities. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of Public Health Nurses in the PHC setting?

options.A: Treating critical injuries in intensive care units
options.B: The health of entire communities and population-level disease prevention
options.C: Performing complex plastic surgeries in tertiary centers

explanation: Public Health Nurses focus on population-level health, disease prevention, and health promotion rather than just individual bedside care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following activities is typically coordinated by Public Health Nurses in communities?

options.A: Mass immunization campaigns and school health programs
options.D: Construction of primary health care physical buildings

explanation: PHNs lead community-based initiatives such as mass immunizations, school health programs, and maternal and child health services. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary responsibility of midwives in the PHC system?

options.A: Providing safe pregnancy, childbirth, and postnatal care for mothers and newborns
options.B: Managing environmental sanitation and waste disposal systems
options.D: Administering vaccinations exclusively to adult male populations

explanation: Midwives focus on maternal and child health, managing antenatal care, normal deliveries, and postnatal recovery. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h5)

question: How do midwives contribute to reducing maternal and neonatal mortality in rural areas?

options.A: By identifying high-risk pregnancies and executing timely emergency referrals when complications arise
options.B: By discouraging women from visiting health facilities
options.C: By treating infectious diseases like malaria exclusively with local herbs
options.D: By focusing only on administrative record-keeping

explanation: Midwives reduce mortality by providing skilled intrapartum care and quickly recognizing and referring obstetric emergencies. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h5)

question: What distinguishes Senior CHEWs from Junior CHEWs in the PHC structure?

options.A: Senior CHEWs have broader training enabling them to manage more advanced tasks and supervise Junior CHEWs
options.B: Junior CHEWs perform major surgeries while Senior CHEWs do administrative work
options.C: Junior CHEWs work only in tertiary teaching hospitals
options.D: Senior CHEWs do not participate in community health delivery

explanation: Senior CHEWs undergo more extensive training allowing them to handle broader clinical tasks and supervise Junior CHEWs at health posts. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is a primary duty typically handled by Junior CHEWs at health posts?

options.A: Routine immunization and treating minor ailments like uncomplicated malaria

explanation: Junior CHEWs focus on foundational tasks such as routine immunization, growth monitoring, and treating minor ailments at the community level. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h6)

question: Who selects Village Health Workers (VHWs) to serve in their communities?

options.B: The Federal Ministry of Health headquarters

explanation: VHWs are voluntary health agents chosen directly by their own community members to represent and support local health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is a core responsibility of a Village Health Worker?

options.A: Promoting basic hygiene, distributing preventive items, and mobilizing for health campaigns
options.D: Managing financial accounts of comprehensive health centers

explanation: VHWs focus on promoting hygiene, distributing items like mosquito nets, providing first aid, and mobilizing communities for health campaigns. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h7)

question: How do Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs) typically acquire their skills?

options.A: Through indigenous traditions, cultural beliefs, and apprenticeship
options.B: Through formal university nursing and medical degrees
options.C: By completing specialized public health master's programs
options.D: Through mandatory residency training in tertiary hospitals

explanation: TBAs acquire their caregiving knowledge from traditional practices, cultural heritage, and community-based apprenticeship rather than formal medical school. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary public health objective regarding TBAs in the Nigerian PHC framework?

options.A: Training them to recognize danger signs and promptly refer high-risk cases to formal health facilities
options.B: Banning them from ever interacting with pregnant women
options.C: Appointing them as directors of tertiary medical centers
options.D: Replacing them with automated medical equipment in villages

explanation: Public health strategies involve training TBAs to identify obstetric danger signs and ensure timely referrals of complicated cases to professional care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why is interprofessional collaboration essential among PHC workers?

options.A: To prevent role confusion, minimize medical errors, and provide holistic care through shared expertise
options.B: So that nurses can perform duties assigned exclusively to doctors without consultation
options.C: To eliminate the need for community health workers in rural clinics
options.D: To increase administrative bureaucracy within local government offices

explanation: Collaboration ensures that diverse healthcare providers respect each other's scopes of practice, communicate effectively, and deliver comprehensive patient care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h9)

question: What is the primary purpose of the referral system in Primary Health Care?

options.A: To ensure structured and smooth patient transfer from lower-level facilities to higher centers when specialized care is needed
options.B: To permanently discharge patients from the healthcare system
options.C: To restrict rural patients from ever seeing a physician
options.D: To increase the workload of primary health workers unnecessarily

explanation: The referral system connects basic health facilities with secondary and tertiary hospitals to ensure patients receive advanced care during emergencies. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h9)
